subject: home ranges from fixed location stations

messages.author: c75afcf4ba885f1f
messages.subject: home ranges from fixed location stations
parts:
Hi Chris, 

Am wondering if you've had much use of ctmm from data collected as animal move through fixed point locations on a grid, rather than collar devices? The data is still sequential and ordered in time, but it's obviously a bit different as instead of the location being sampled at given time intervals, you can only locate the individual when they pass by the stations. 

Have plotted out variograms of the data, and you see a nice asymptote over time, was wondering about how you would move forward with, say home ranges, for this kind of data. For example, if weighting would be beneficial or not, as the irregularity in the time sampling is from a different process than, say, changes in duty cycles. 

Thanks!

Gen

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: home ranges from fixed location stations
parts:
Hi Gen,

The proper way to analyze this kind of data is with a model like this: https://movementecologyjournal.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s40462-020-00199-6
The observation model is very different than GPS/Argos/VHF currently supported by ctmm. I'd like to get support into ctmm, but that will be a major effort (possibly in the next grant).

If you put this kind of data into location tracking methods, then the results become bad when the scales of movement are smaller than or comparable to the the grid resolution. So for coarse data, an (A)KDE home-range estimate might look okay if the bandwidth > grid scale, but with more data, you will start to see excess density at the stations.

Best,
Chris

Hi Chris, 

Thanks for the link -- really neat stuff!

Have been so wrapped up in tracking movement models recently, hadn't even thought about that, I guess it's more like camera trap data in many ways -- will definitely look into that. If you did use this kind of data for (A)KDE, presumably the finest spatial scale you can resolve HR estimates for would be linked to the spatial resolution of the station grid? Would it, therefore, make sense to hard code this in, using the grid argument?

Gen

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: home ranges from fixed location stations
parts:
Hi Gen,

I guess you could try fitting with location error equal to the detection radius, and then taking the maximum of the optimal bandwidth (under the wrong observation model) and the spatial resolution of the station grid. Then there are internal functions that you could use to create the density estimate given an arbitrary bandwidth (or another package like ks).

I've also been talking to someone with mark-capture-recapture data about taking the (A)KDE PDF evaluated at the stations, interpolating those point estimates over the whole domain, and then renormalizing the interpolated density to integrate to 1. That would at least give you something that is asymptotically consistent at the station locations and smoothly varying between.

Best,
Chris
